VI.description: PURPOSE\0ASimulates what an e-bike motor controller (MCU) would report on CAN\2C so the eDyno PoC can log electrical and thermal channels next to vibration. Feeds the MCU_Status frame (0x300) through eDyno CAN Pack Signals.vi. It is a simple STEADY-STATE model for demos - not a validated motor model.\0A\0AINPUTS\0A- Speed (rpm)\3A shaft speed (the simulator's Shaft Speed).\0A- Load Torque (Nm)\3A torque at the motor shaft. Positive = motoring\2C negative = regen. Typical e-bike mid-drive cruise 0.3-1 Nm at the motor shaft (before the gearbox).\0A- Motor Parameters\3A defaults describe a generic 250-500 W\2C 36 V\2C 4-pole-pair mid-drive motor. Change them to match a real motor.\0A\0AOUTPUT (MCU Status cluster\2C same order as the CAN signals)\0AMotor Speed\2C Torque\2C Phase Current RMS\2C DC Voltage\2C DC Current\2C Electrical Power\2C Winding Temp\2C Controller Temp.\0A\0AEQUATIONS (one labelled frame each on the block diagram)\0A1) omega = rpm x 2pi/60; P_mech = T x omega\0A2) I_ph = I_noload + |T|/Kt; P_copper = 3 x R_ph x I_ph^2; P_iron+friction = k x rpm; P_loss = sum\0A3) P_elec = P_mech + P_loss; V_dc = V_batt - R_batt x P_elec/V_batt; I_dc = P_elec/V_dc\0A4) T_winding = T_amb + Rth_w x P_loss; T_controller = T_amb + Rth_c x |P_elec|\0A\0AEXAMPLE (defaults)\3A 4500 rpm\2C 0.5 Nm -> 11.5 A rms\2C 273 W\2C 35.6 V\2C 7.7 A DC\2C winding 47.7 degC\2C controller 35.9 degC.\0A\0ALIMITATIONS\0ATemperatures jump instantly (no thermal time constant); efficiency map is approximate; field weakening\2C voltage limit and current limit are not modelled.

Structure.label: 4) STEADY-STATE TEMPERATURES (no thermal lag)\0AT_winding [degC] = T_ambient + Rth_winding x P_loss\0AT_controller [degC] = T_ambient + Rth_controller x |P_elec|
3) ELECTRICAL INPUT (BATTERY SIDE)\0AP_elec [W] = P_mech + P_loss (negative = regen)\0AV_dc [V] = V_batt - R_batt x (P_elec / V_batt)\0AI_dc [A] = P_elec / V_dc
2) PHASE CURRENT AND LOSSES\0AI_ph [A rms] = I_noload + |Torque| / Kt\0AP_copper [W] = 3 x R_ph x I_ph^2\0AP_iron+friction [W] = k x rpm\0AP_loss = P_copper + P_iron+friction
1) MECHANICAL POWER\0Aomega [rad/s] = rpm x 2pi/60\0AP_mech [W] = Torque x omega
